question: Can one 1/300 s physics clock and one common control rate serve both robots without hiding a tracking, learning, safety, or throughput regression?

invariants.source_clock: Each clip retains its own source_fps; reference lookup interpolates in seconds and never rewrites source rows.
invariants.final_state: Exact pre-reset reached observation is required on every done edge; fallback count must remain zero.
invariants.robot: Asset, actuator, body order, joint order, controller gains, action normalization, and observation routes remain robot-preset data.
invariants.data: The same source split, clip order, materialized bank hash, reset mixture, and evaluation initial states are used within each robot comparison.
invariants.reward_boundary: Environment reward remains a density multiplied by control_dt exactly once by RewardManager; stored auxiliary evidence remains raw.
invariants.discount_rule: Every Bellman target, helper critic, and return estimator uses gamma_new = exp(log(gamma_native) * control_dt_new / control_dt_native).
invariants.target_updates: Polyak rates and update counts are frozen per gradient update; update-to-transition ratio is reported and never silently retimed.
invariants.randomness: Common seeds and evaluation initial states are paired within robot; cross-robot values are not paired observations.

native_discount.warning: Equal native gamma does not mean equal physical discount horizon because the control periods differ.

comparison_order.purpose: Isolate integration/contact/actuator sensitivity while retaining each native control period.
Measure controller and observation/action sampling sensitivity before retraining.
Train only after deterministic tracking and reward-discretization checks pass.

reward_discretization_gate.environment_scalar: Already a physical-time density integral because RewardManager multiplies by control_dt.
reward_discretization_gate.auxiliary_evidence: No blanket dt scaling is allowed. Each channel must declare whether it is a density, impulse, state occupancy cost, or finite difference before a changed-control-rate learning comparison.
reward_discretization_gate.action_rate: Must be derived against elapsed seconds or explicitly retained as a per-action source objective; these are different experiments.
reward_discretization_gate.changed_control_rows: Report both source-objective and physically normalized variants if channel semantics permit both; do not merge them.

decision.eligibility: A common timing candidate is eligible only if both robots separately pass predeclared native-relative tracking, learning, safety, and systems gates.
